payload.text:
You are an expert Product Manager, Full-Stack Engineer, UX/UI Designer, and RAG Architect.

Design and generate a production-ready web application using Google AI Studio (Gemini / Nano Banana compatible) called:

“Industry Insight Studio”

The application allows customers to:
1) Input research requirements to generate professional industry reports
2) Upload market documents and provide market-related URLs
3) Let the AI learn from those sources using a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline
4) Generate reports with cited evidence and summaries

==================================================
1. Product Objectives
==================================================
Build a customer-facing AI research platform that:

- Accepts structured research inputs:
  - Industry / Topic
  - Focus areas (multi-select)
  - Target audience
  - Geography
  - Time horizon (current / last 12–24 months / 3–5 year outlook)
  - Report depth (brief / standard / deep professional)
  - Use case (investment, strategy, marketing, internal planning)
  - Output language and format

- Accepts knowledge sources:
  A) Uploaded documents (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, TXT, CSV, MD)
  B) Market information URLs (news, research pages, competitors, policy sites)

- Uses RAG to:
  - Ingest, index, and retrieve relevant content
  - Generate industry reports grounded in customer-provided sources
  - Attach citations to each major conclusion

==================================================
2. UI / UX Requirements (Design in AI Studio)
==================================================
Overall style:
- Modern, professional, tech-forward
- Clean card-based layout
- Light / Dark mode toggle
- Rounded corners, soft shadows
- Font: Inter (or similar modern sans-serif)
- Fully responsive (desktop + mobile)

--------------------------------------------------
A) Main Page — “Generate Report”
--------------------------------------------------
Layout:
- Left panel: Research input form
- Right panel: Output tabs

Research Input Fields:
- Industry / Topic (required)
- Focus Areas (checkboxes):
  - Market size & growth
  - Competitive landscape
  - Technology trends
  - Policy & regulation
  - Business models
  - Investment opportunities
  - Risks & challenges
- Target Audience (dropdown)
- Geography (dropdown + custom)
- Time Horizon (dropdown)
- Report Depth (dropdown)
- Output Language (EN / CN)
- Output Format (Markdown / Word-style / PPT outline)
- Additional Notes (optional)

Output Tabs:
1) Industry Report (structured, copyable)
2) Executive Summary (1-page)
3) Evidence & Citations
   - Source type (Document / URL)
   - Title or file name
   - Page / section reference
   - Quoted excerpt
   - Clickable link (for URLs)
4) PPT-Ready Key Takeaways (10–15 bullets)

--------------------------------------------------
B) Knowledge Base (Documents)
--------------------------------------------------
Features:
- Upload documents
- View document list:
  - File name
  - Type
  - Size
  - Upload time
  - Parsing status
  - Indexing status
- Preview extracted text
- Re-index or delete documents
- Organize documents by Project / Workspace
- Enforce limits:
  - Max files per project
  - Max file size

--------------------------------------------------
C) URL Sources
--------------------------------------------------
Features:
- Paste multiple URLs (one per line)
- Crawl current page only (default)
- Show crawl status:
  - Pending / Processing / Success / Failed
- Display:
  - Page title
  - Word count
  - Last fetched time
- Allow re-crawl and delete
- Tag URLs (e.g., competitor, regulation, pricing, news)

--------------------------------------------------
D) History & Export
--------------------------------------------------
- Save each report generation as a version:
  - Timestamp
  - Input parameters
  - Number of sources used
  - Model version
- Export formats:
  - Markdown
  - PDF
  - DOCX
- Support report version comparison (highlight differences)

--------------------------------------------------
E) Settings / Admin (Optional)
--------------------------------------------------
- Role-based access:
  - Owner / Admin / Member / Viewer
- Viewer:
  - Can view reports only
  - Cannot upload or delete sources
- Configure:
  - File limits
  - URL crawl rules
  - Chunk size
  - Retrieval Top-K

==================================================
3. RAG Architecture (Explainable)
==================================================
Ingestion:
- Parse documents and web pages into clean text
- Chunking strategy:
  - 800–1200 tokens
  - 80–120 token overlap
- Generate embeddings for each chunk
- Store metadata:
  - source_type (file / url)
  - source_name
  - url (if applicable)
  - page or section
  - project_id
  - content_hash (deduplication)

Retrieval:
- Construct multiple retrieval queries from:
  - Topic
  - Focus areas
  - Geography
  - Time horizon
- Retrieve Top-K relevant chunks (8–15)
- Inject retrieved context into the LLM

Generation Rules:
- Base all factual claims on retrieved content
- Every major insight must include at least one citation
- Clearly label assumptions where data is inferred

==================================================
4. Report Output Structure (Mandatory)
==================================================
The generated industry report must include:

1. Executive Summary
2. Industry Definition & Scope
3. Market Overview & Current State
4. Key Trends & Developments
5. Competitive Landscape
6. Policy & External Environment (if applicable)
7. Opportunities & Risks
8. Future Outlook (3–5 years)
9. Strategic Recommendations (tailored to target audience)

==================================================
5. Output Quality Standards
==================================================
- Professional, neutral, and decision-ready
- Suitable for executives and investors
- Avoid casual language
- Clearly distinguish:
  - Facts
  - Analysis
  - Assumptions
- Ready to be used in:
  - Investment memos
  - Strategy decks
  - Whitepapers
  - Client deliverables

==================================================
Begin designing the application and generating the UI and system logic.
==================================================

**Formulating the Concept**

I'm solidifying the vision for "Industry Insight Studio."  The core is a B2B React application, expertly blending AI and RAG. I'm focusing on the user's need for a robust platform to generate industry reports.  Currently, I'm working to nail down the precise features within the research input form.


**Detailing the Architecture**

I've significantly expanded the architecture for "Industry Insight Studio."  The design is becoming clearer, particularly regarding the user input and output. I've focused on integrating the Gemini API and defining the React components for the report tabs.  I'm also setting up the backend structure for input sources (files and URLs) and report generation logic.


**Clarifying Presentation**

I've simplified the formatting approach. I'm opting for clean text and `white-space: pre-wrap` for the professional look, rather than introducing markdown parsing complexities.  This aligns nicely with the streamlined architecture I'm building.


**Simulating RAG Logic**

I'm now concentrating on simulating the RAG process within the client-side demo.  I've devised a clear plan for handling user-added sources (files and URLs) by simulating content extraction and fetching, due to client-side constraints.  I'll use the user's topic description alongside the source text as context for the Gemini API. To optimize speed and quality, I plan to utilize the `gemini-2.5-flash-preview` or `gemini-3-flash-preview` models, ensuring the generated reports meet specific section requirements through a structured prompt.


**Enhancing Presentation Design**

I'm solidifying the presentation, focusing on a professional color scheme, and the plan is to stick with a "Slate" or "Zinc" palette in Tailwind for the dark/light modes. Also, I've clarified how the sources will be added to the prompt, e.g. CONTEXT DATA: [Source 1 content] [Source 2 content], and how citations will be handled and displayed in an "Evidence" tab.

I've also refined the overall prompt strategy. Aiming for a structured JSON output with Gemini, I'm setting the stage to use `gemini-3-flash-preview` for high quality, professional-grade reports. The focus remains on generating content for tabs for easy consumption.


**Organizing the Architecture**

I'm now concretizing the application architecture, focusing on key components. I'll utilize a `GeminiService` with a JSON response schema for efficient report generation. On the UI side, I'm developing components like `Sidebar`, `ResearchForm`, `SourceManager`, and `ReportOutput`.  Main app logic will manage the current view and source list. I'm also ensuring the design is mobile-first, and will use Tailwind and standard HTML file inputs, avoiding third-party libraries. I've considered default mock sources as a fallback.


**Structuring the Application**

I'm now deep in the codebase, building out the file structure. I'm focusing on key UI components and services, ensuring clear separation of concerns. The `geminiService` is taking shape to handle the API interactions. I'm excited about the JSON output schema, which will streamline report presentation, and I'm ready to populate the UI tabs.

## Random Forest with Hyperparameter Tuning using Grid Search

In []:
```python
# perform Grid Search to find the best hyperparameters for Random Forest
# the values were chosen to be close to the default values
# n_estimators: Number of trees in the forest.
# max_depth: Maximum depth of the trees.
# min_samples_split: Minimum number of samples required to split an internal node.
# min_samples_leaf: Minimum number of samples required at a leaf node.
# max_features: Number of features to consider when looking for the best split.

param_grid = {
    'n_estimators': [50, 100, 200],
    'max_depth': [None, 10, 20],
    'min_samples_split': [2, 5, 10],
    'min_samples_leaf': [1, 2, 4],
    'max_features': ['sqrt', 'log2']
}

grid_search = GridSearchCV(RandomForestClassifier(random_state=42), param_grid, cv=5, scoring='accuracy', n_jobs=-1)
grid_search.fit(X_train, y_train)

# get the best model
best_rf = grid_search.best_params_
print(f"Best Hyperparameters: {best_rf}")

```

## Comparing Model Results

The table below shows the results of the 6 models created: Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines, Decision Tree, Random Forest, AdaBoost, and XGBoost.

| Model | Accuracy | Precision | Recall | F1-Score | Log-loss |
|-------|----------|-----------|--------|----------|----------|
| Logistic Regression | 0.826 | 0.814 | 0.778 | 0.795 | 0.435 |

In []:
Comparing these models, the **Support Vector Machine (SVM)** stands out as the best performer across most metrics on the test data. It achieved the highest accuracy (0.837), precision (0.822), recall (0.822), and F1-score (0.822). Additionally, it had the lowest log-loss (0.384), indicating more confident and accurate probability predictions. Logistic Regression also performed well, while ensemble methods like Random Forest and XGBoost showed slightly lower performance on this specific dataset. The Decision Tree's high log-loss (6.657) suggests that while its classifications are decent, its confidence in those classifications is poor, making it less robust than the other models.

In []:
## Discussion

In []:
Based on the results of the model comparisons, I would recommend using the **Support Vector Machine (SVM)** model for this heart disease prediction task. It provided the highest overall accuracy and F1-score, and it also had the lowest log-loss, indicating that its probability estimates are the most reliable.

The high performance of SVM and Logistic Regression suggests that the relationship between the features and the target variable is relatively linear or can be well-captured with a radial basis function kernel in the case of SVM. Ensemble methods like Random Forest and XGBoost, while powerful, might be slightly overfitting or not as well-suited for this particular dataset's size and feature characteristics.

However, a critical factor in a medical diagnostic tool is the balance between precision and recall. High recall is particularly important because it ensures that most patients with heart disease are correctly identified (low false negatives). SVM's recall of 0.822 is the highest among all models, making it the most suitable choice from a clinical perspective.

Further steps to improve the model could include:
- Exploring more advanced feature engineering.
- Increasing the dataset size if possible.
- Fine-tuning the SVM further with a broader range of hyperparameters in a grid search.
- Investigating the misclassified cases to see if there are common patterns the model is missing.

Allow users to provide external web sources that the system can reference, analyze, and cite during research and content generation.

Requirements:
- Users may manually input external URLs as reference sources.
- The system must allow a maximum of FIVE (5) URLs per research session or project.
- URLs must be publicly accessible (no login required).
- Each URL should be fetched, parsed, and stored as a reference source.
- The system should retain the URL metadata:
  - URL
  - Page title (if available)
  - Last fetched timestamp

- If the user attempts to add more than 5 URLs, show a clear warning:
  “You can add up to 5 reference URLs.”
- Duplicate URLs should be automatically detected and rejected.
- Invalid or unreachable URLs should return a user-friendly error message.

Usage:
- Global Sources URLs are used as reference material for:
  - Research analysis
  - Evidence citation
  - Social media content generation
  - Visual generation context
- The system must be able to reference these URLs when generating insights or evidence sections.

================================================

================================================

Purpose:
Allow users to upload proprietary or curated documents that serve as private knowledge sources for the research process.

- Duplicate files (based on file hash) should be automatically detected and rejected.
- Unsupported file types should be blocked with a clear error message.

Usage:
- Knowledge Base documents are used as private context for:
  - Industry research analysis
  - Report generation
  - Evidence extraction
  - Social content and visual generation
- These documents must not be exposed publicly or shared outside the user’s workspace.

================================================
3. UX & Feedback Requirements
================================================

- Display a clear counter for both sections:
  - “Global Sources: 3 / 5 URLs added”
  - “Knowledge Base: 2 / 5 documents uploaded”
- Disable the “Add” or “Upload” action once the limit is reached.
- Provide clear, non-technical feedback messages for validation errors.

================================================
4. Performance & Quality Constraints
================================================

- Input limits are enforced to:
  - Maintain system performance

The need for real-time synchronization and the ability to query specific report segments are key factors in my decision.


**Deciding Persistence Strategy**

**Selecting Primary Persistence**

For a production-grade RAG platform like **CrestPoint AI Brain**, I recommend **Supabase** over Google Drive. 

As a RAG Architect, here is why:
1. **Vector Storage:** Supabase supports `pgvector`, allowing you to store document embeddings directly in your database for high-speed semantic search.
2. **Relational Metadata:** You can link citations, research projects, and social media drafts to specific users and sources in a structured way.
3. **Performance:** Querying a SQL database is significantly faster than traversing a Google Drive folder structure for every research request.

**Analyzing Base64 Usage**

I'm now zeroing in on the base64 implementation. My analysis shows its presence in both image generation (Gemini service) and visual asset previews (ReportView). I need to understand its exact role in these UI/UX flows.


**Exploring Encoding Mechanisms**

I've been exploring Base64 encoding further, focusing on its mechanism and its relevance in our web development context.  My understanding is that it transforms binary data into text, crucial for embedding images or other binary assets within text-based formats like JSON or HTML.  The connection to Gemini's image generation process, where images are returned as Base64 strings, and subsequently turned into data URIs for display, is now quite clear.

Base64 is an encoding scheme used to represent binary data (like images, videos, or files) as a string of **plain text characters**. In the context of your application and the Gemini API, here is why it matters: ### 1. How it works It takes binary data (0s and 1s) and translates it into a set of 64 printable characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, +, and /). For example, a tiny image that a computer sees as raw bytes might look like this in Base64: `iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mP8/5+hHgAHggJ/PchI7wAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==` ### 2. Why we use it in this app * **Image Generation:** When you ask Gemini to generate an image for social media, the API sends the image back as a long Base64 string. * **Data URIs:** Your browser can't directly "read" raw binary code in an `` tag. By prefixing the Base64 string with `data:image/png;base64,`, we create a **Data URI**. This allows the browser to display the image without needing to host a separate file on a server. * **JSON Transport:** JSON (the format the API uses to talk to your app) can only handle text. Base64 allows us to "hide" a complex image file inside a simple text field so it can be sent over the internet easily. ### 3. Pros and Cons * **Pro:** It makes it very easy to move images around as simple text. No need for complex file management systems for small assets. * **Con:** Base64 strings are about **33% larger** than the original binary file. This is why it's great for social media thumbnails and report images, but not ideal for very large high-definition videos. **In short:** Base64 is the "language" used to turn the AI's visual creations into text that your code can handle and your browser can show.
